Nagpaabot ng iba-ibang tulong-medikal ang QC Health Department sa mga residenteng naapektuhan ng nangyaring sunog sa San Roque St., Riverside Ext., Brgy. Commonwealth.

Sanib-pwersa ang QC Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office, QC Fire Department, Social Services Development Department, Traffic & Transport Management Department, Department of Public Order & Safety, City Veterinary Department, QC Health Department, QC Police District, at barangay officials upang magbigay ng ayuda at relief services sa mga nasunugan.

Lima ang naitalang nasugatan habang umabot naman sa 70 pamilya ang apektado ng sunog na pansamantalang nanunuluyan sa San Pascual open court, Unit 4 Plaza, at Bato-Bato covered court.

WATER SHORTAGE IN CARMEN?

SILOY IS WATCHING: A Ka-Siloy from Carmen, Cebu, told CDN Digital that the town has faced a lack of water supply for two days. The resident shared photos taken on Monday, December 29, showing households waiting as personnel distributed water from fire trucks.

The resident said the shortage is not new and persists although Carmen is a main water source for Metro Cebu.

“Dili lang ni siya first time nahitabo. Pila na katuig ning problema sa tubig sa lungsod sa Carmen. Grabe ang kasagmuyo nga nabati sa nga tawo sa lungsod tungod kay mag bag-ong tuig na pero wala miy tubig,” the resident added.

(This isn’t the first time this has happened. The water problem in the town of Carmen has been going on for years. Residents are extremely frustrated because the New Year is approaching, yet we still don’t have water.)

Earlier today, the Municipality of Carmen’s Public Information Office posted an advisory explaining that a malfunction at a Manila Water pump has slowed water supply in several areas. The PIO said fire trucks were scheduled to provide temporary relief while officials monitor the situation. | 📷: Contributed photos via Ian Peter Guanzon #CDNDigital #SiloyIsWatching
